item.content:encoded:
Here are a few suggestions:

  • "SCP-3178 is seasoning which consists of the composition normally found in factory-made monosodium glutamate with the addition of an unidentified substance." -> "SCP-3178 is a seasoning consisting of factory-made monosodium glutamate and an unidentified substance." It's a minor prose nitpick, but excessive prepositional phrases hurt your clarity and conciseness. I have the same problem, and recommend running your writing through Slickwrite.com to catch it.
  • "the balanced flavour of SCP-3178" is a bit too subjective for my liking. Also, the author can't really know that unless they also tasted it. Maybe say that subjects report the flavor as balanced.
  • "SCP-3178 consumers lose the part of the brain" feels weird. Does that part just cease to exist? It might make more sense to say that it deteriorates
  • SCP-3178-1 feel really disconnected from the rest of the SCP. I'd either remove them or find a way to more smoothly incorporate them.
  • Test logs are good, but a couple of them seem a bit repetitive, maybe remove a couple

On the whole, I think the concept definitely has potential, but there are too many issues for me to give it a +1, so I'm going to make it a non-vote.

item.title: Ditto except +1
item.content:encoded: I deciced to put this as a reply because I agree with Tomato’s comments- the article is just… weird. It’s a bunch of stuff all put together that doesn’t make sense, and frankly I like the feeling that some SCP’s are nested enigmas of randomness with only hints at central causes. Maybe it’s a take on a myth, maybe you went to randomwordgenerator.com and got MSG, addiction, eyebrow, and elf. Maybe it’s Maybelline. But imho it’s a breath of fresh air to see some plain, old-fashioned weird $#!*. +1 for good execution on a weird idea.

item.content:encoded:
My biggest problem with this article is that I can't find any thread of cohesiveness. It's ramen flavoring that tastes really good and is addictive, also it makes the eater dumb (didn't we get something like that from 294 once?), also there are physical effects that don't seem to have any relation to the object, and there are elderly toddlers following people around and stealing their stuff to purchase ramen I guess? Are they purchasing it from the eater, or is it for the eater to purchase more ramen? Either way, none of the article fits together and I'm just left with a bunch of questions. And not the good kind of questions.

-1

item.content:encoded: In the test logs you should use metric units, especially as it's not clear whether you mean fluid ounces or ounces by weight. Either way 12 ounces of table salt would be lethal unless immediately regurgitated (unless I missed something). A few tablespoons is enough to threaten a grown adult of average height and weight. Again, I may have missed where you mentioned an anomalous resistance to hypernatremia, but that's a lot of salt. The gastric distress from trying to eat a handful of black pepper goes without mentioning.
